title: Graceful name mapping and call fallback shim for mixed tool/function surfaces
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: Redwood currently exposes two overlapping call surfaces: the newer OpenAI-style 'tools' contract and older 'legacy function' payloads used by early customers and some partner SDKs. Model prompts and third-party agents may produce tool names or function signatures that differ by casing, punctuation, or legacy prefixes, causing failed calls or incorrect fallbacks. Goals: 1) Provide a runtime shim that normalizes tool/function names and resolves the best matching implementation at call time. 2) Implement deterministic fallback ordering (exact->normalized->legacy-signature->proxy) with telemetry and opt-in strict mode. 3) Avoid behavioral regressions for current customers and keep performance impact under 5% p50 latency. Non-goals: redesigning the tool contract or changing public SDKs' canonical names in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a name-mapper module that returns a ranked list of candidate implementations for a given incoming tool name or function signature
Default fallback order implemented: exact match -> normalized match (case/whitespace/punctuation) -> legacy mapping table -> runtime proxy to legacy function runtime
Telemetry emitted for resolution path (fields: incoming_name, resolved_key, resolution_reason, latency_ms)
Unit and integration tests covering 100+ fuzzy-match cases including unicode, punctuation, and common legacy prefixes
E2E smoke test demonstrating <5% median latency regression under a synthetic tool-calling workload
Feature flag/tenant config exists to enforce strict matching semantics for customers that opt-in
Canary rollout plan documented and validated for Dedicated and Private deployments
implementation_notes: Name normalization rules: lowercasing, collapse whitespace, remove non-alphanumeric except '_' and '-' , map common prefixes (eg 'fn_' -> '')
Maintain a static legacy mapping table (config-driven) that maps old function signatures to current tool keys; loadable from S3/ConfigService
Resolution algorithm: compile candidate list once per request; attempt resolution synchronously; if unresolved and tenant allows, proxy call to legacy runtime with a retry budget
Performance: cache resolved mappings per model/tenant for 10m with LRU to avoid repeated compute
Fallback safety: throttle proxy fallback to avoid cascading costs; add quota and circuit-breaker metrics
APIs: add 'resolution_hint' field to call response metadata for Debuggable responses; ensure not returned by default in prod unless debug header present
Opt-in strict_mode: when enabled, unresolved names return 400 with helpful error and suggestion list instead of proxying
testing_plan: Integration tests using local runtime proxy that simulates legacy function surface
Load test with k6 measuring p50/p95 token latency before/after change
Compatibility test matrix: combinations of model (gpt-like open models), tokenization differences, and client SDK variations
QA checklist for Dedicated and Private: config rollout, permission checks, KMS access for legacy runtime if proxied
rollout_plan: Developer canary: enable flag for infra team in staging for 48h
Internal beta: enable for 10 internal customers and Redwood-managed demo accounts
Gradual ramp: increase tenant percentage by 10% every 24h while monitoring errors and latency
Full rollout: after 7 days of stable metrics, flip default on for hosted; Dedicated/Private via release notes and config
Rollback: feature-flag off reverts behavior to exact-match-only semantics
metrics_and_alerts: Metric: tool_resolution_success_rate by tenant and model
Alert: proxy_error_rate spike > 0.5% of tool calls (P2)
Dashboard: top 20 unresolved incoming_names with sample requests and suggested mappings
